summary: Overlapping route patterns causing double-counted quota and persistent 429 responses
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a spike of 429 throttling errors across multiple endpoints after deploying new route patterns to isolate background flushers from interactive traffic. Impact: Persistent 429s for interactive requests during normal traffic (5-10% error rate for tenant), leading to user-visible failures in document preview and search. Environment: Dedicated pool, prod:us-east, tenant bound to dedicated pool. Observed behavior: Many requests show quota token consumption that appears to be applied twice per incoming request (route-level and route-variant match), exhausting route-specific burst credits quickly. Expected behavior: Each incoming request should decrement tenant quota exactly once; route isolation should prevent low-priority background flushers from affecting interactive route quotas.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer created two overlapping route patterns: /api/documents/* (interactive) and /api/documents/uploads/* (background flush).
2) Configured per-route quotas with a low burst allowance for the uploads route and a higher burst for interactive route.
3) Started background flush job that performs parallel multipart uploads to /api/documents/uploads/* while interactive traffic continues.
4) Observed elevated 429 responses for interactive requests after ~10 minutes; quota console shows rapid depletion on the interactive route despite volume fitting configured thresholds.
logs:
Sample request traces: 
- 2026-03-12T14:05:21Z tenant=nimbledocs request_id=abc123 path=/api/documents/preview token_deducted=2 route_matches=[/api/documents/*, /api/documents/uploads/*] policy=per-route-burst status=429
- 2026-03-12T14:05:22Z tenant=nimbledocs request_id=abc124 path=/api/documents/uploads/part token_deducted=1 route_matches=[/api/documents/uploads/*] status=200
Rate-limiter debug (sample): new_token_count=-1 after deduction (expected >=0). Edge proxy logs show duplicate match entries for some requests when route regexes overlap. Full trace links: https://logs.redwood.internal/trace/abc123 (customer tenant scoped link provided).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: overlapping route regexes are causing the request to be counted against both route buckets when the routing layer emits multiple matches rather than choosing a single best-match.
Verified console: per-route quota counters incremented twice for a subset of interactive requests; ingress request inspection shows two matched routes recorded on the request metadata.

Reproduced in staging: created same pair of route patterns, ran synthetic parallel uploads and interactive calls — saw same double-accounting behavior when route ordering was not longest-prefix-first.

Root cause candidate: routing precedence change in recent edge-proxy release allowed multiple matches to be returned for instrumentation; the rate-limiter then applied quota deductions for each matched route without deduplicating by request ID and best-match selection.
Risk assessment: high for dedicated tenants relying on per-route isolation; may lead to persistent 429s and SLA violations during background flush windows.
comments: Priya Shah (Support) - 2026-03-12: Logged by customer after spike observed during scheduled flush. Attached example trace and console snapshot. Requested triage for P1 impact.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Acknowledged and started reproduction in staging. Noted edge-proxy change two days ago. Will instrument internal rate-limiter to log match counts per request.

Eng (Routing) - 2026-03-13: Confirmed change in edge-proxy returns all matching routes when advanced_match flag is enabled. Rate-limiter assumed single match. Created INT-5521 to add defensive dedupe logic in rate-limiter and push validation to Console route editor.
NimbleDocs (Customer) - 2026-03-13: Provided topology and background flush schedule. Customer asks for immediate mitigation while engineering ships fix.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) - 2026-03-14: Temporary mitigation applied: disabled advanced_match flag for the customer's ingress host to restore longest-prefix single-match behavior. Monitoring shows 429s dropping to baseline. Preparing patch for dedupe logic.
resolution: Mitigation and permanent fix plan: 1) Immediate mitigation: rolled back advanced matching flag for tenant ingress (2026-03-14 03:20 UTC) — interactive 429s reduced to baseline within 10 minutes. 2) Engineering fix: added deduplication guard in rate-limiter to collapse multiple matched routes to a single best-match before quota deduction (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1983). 3) Console validation: added preflight validation in route editor to warn on overlapping patterns with different quotas and recommend explicit isolation. 4) Post-action: created follow-up internal task INT-5521 to add unit tests and rollout plan across dedicated pools. Customer confirmed functionality restored and will monitor during next scheduled flush. Follow-ups: document pattern in support KB and include example config to avoid overlap.
